name: Charles Darwin National Park
coordinates_source: OSM tourism=information board inside the park (visitor entrance area, Wishart Road side); park centroid not used
bio: Small national park south-east of the city with World War II bunkers, city lookouts, middens and fire trails.
source_note: National park 4 km south-east of Darwin with WWII concrete bunkers (one a visitor centre), city lookouts, middens and fire trails; a park, but small, so a stop, not a destination.

name: Fogg Dam Conservation Reserve
coordinates_source: OSM tourism=viewpoint on the dam wall; the Commons photo median is 40 m away
bio: Wetland reserve with bird-watching hides along a narrow road across Fogg Dam, rich in birdlife.
source_note: Wetland conservation reserve with bird-watching hides along a narrow road across Fogg Dam, free entry, rich birdlife per Wikivoyage.

name: The Big Boxing Crocodile
bio: Roadside giant sculpture of a boxing crocodile on the Arnhem Highway at Humpty Doo, one of Australia's big things.
source_note: Roadside giant sculpture of a boxing crocodile on the Arnhem Highway at Humpty Doo, one of Australia's big things, open 24/7 per Wikivoyage.

name: Palmerston
bio: Darwin's second centre about 20 km south-east, with shopping, the Palmerston Water Park and the SWELL entertainment venue.
source_note: Growing city about 20 km south-east of Darwin, the region's second centre, with shopping, the Palmerston Water Park and SWELL entertainment venue.

name: Wangi Falls
coordinates_source: photon waterway=waterfall "Wangi Falls"; agrees with wiki, commons
bio: Litchfield's most popular waterfall and swimming hole, with a campground, kiosk and barbecues.
source_note: Waterfall and swimming spot in Litchfield with a campground, kiosk, hot showers and barbecues; Wikivoyage calls it the park's most popular attraction.

name: Florence Falls
coordinates_source: photon waterway=waterfall "Florence Falls"; agrees with photon, commons
bio: Double waterfall in monsoon forest with a plunge pool reached by about 160 steps.
source_note: Double waterfall in monsoon forest in Litchfield with a plunge pool reached by about 160 steps; a headline swim spot.

name: Buley Rockhole
coordinates_source: photon tourism=viewpoint "Buley Rockhole"; agrees with commons
bio: Cascading waterfalls and rockholes a short walk from the car park, popular for swimming.
source_note: Series of cascading waterfalls and rockholes in Litchfield, a short walk from the car park with steps; a swimming spot.

name: Magnetic Termite Mounds
coordinates_source: photon tourism=attraction "Magnetic Termite Mounds"; agrees with photon, commons
bio: Viewing platform over flat-faced magnetic termite mounds aligned north to south.
source_note: Viewing area of magnetic termite mounds in Litchfield, the flat-faced mounds aligned north to south; a short roadside stop with a platform.

name: Tolmer Falls
coordinates_source: photon waterway=waterfall "Tolmer Falls"; agrees with wiki
bio: Waterfall viewing platform over a gorge; the pool is closed to swimmers to protect wildlife.
source_note: Waterfall in Litchfield with a viewing platform over a gorge; Tourism NT lists it as a waterfall viewing spot.

name: Batchelor
bio: Small gateway town to Litchfield with the park's headquarters and Batchelor Museum.
source_note: Small town at the gateway to Litchfield National Park with the Litchfield park headquarters, a butterfly farm and Batchelor Museum; a gateway town.

name: Tabletop Track
coordinates_source: Midpoint of the OSM "Tabletop Track" ways chained west to east (39.6 km of way); OSM has no route relation, so the order is approximate
bio: Walk of about 39 km over three to five days from Wangi Falls to Florence Falls via Walker Creek; permit needed.
source_note: Multi-day bushwalk (about 39 km, three to five days) from Wangi Falls to Florence Falls through Walker Creek, requiring a permit; a long walk route.

name: The Lost City
bio: Sandstone rock formations reached only by a 4WD track, the park's most demanding drive.
source_note: Sandstone rock formations in Litchfield reached only by a 4WD track, the most challenging drive in the park per Wikivoyage.

name: Adelaide River
coordinates_source: photon amenity=police "Adelaide River Police Station"; agrees with wiki
bio: Stuart Highway town about 112 km south of Darwin, base for jumping crocodile cruises and a war cemetery.
source_note: Small town on the Stuart Highway about 112 km south of Darwin, base for jumping crocodile river cruises, the WWII war cemetery and the Adelaide River Inn.

name: Mary River National Park
coordinates_source: OSM tourism=attraction "Corroboree Billabong Wetland Cruises", the park's main visitor access off the Arnhem Highway; park centroid not used
bio: Park of wetlands and billabongs on the Arnhem Highway, known for dense birdlife and crocodile cruises.
source_note: National park of wetlands and billabongs on the Arnhem Highway, famous for dense birdlife and crocodile cruises; a park, too small to be a destination on its own, its spots are Corroboree Billabong and the wetlands.

name: Tiwi Islands
coordinates_source: OSM place=village "Wurrumiyanga" on Bathurst Island, where tours and flights arrive; the Wikipedia point for the island group is open water
bio: Island group north of Darwin with rainforest, beaches, Tiwi art and mission heritage, reached by air or ferry.
source_note: Island group about 80 km north of Darwin (Bathurst and Melville islands and nine smaller islands): rainforest, beaches, Tiwi art and a Catholic mission heritage; reached by air or ferry on an organised tour.
